name: 28-capabilities
note: What the deployment can and cannot collect, BEFORE a session exists. Nowheresville reports as unsupported rather than quietly returning nothing, which is the distinction the endpoint exists to make.

mission.description: Synthetic crowd-convergence mission used by the test suite and by contract generation. Detects a large scheduled gathering forming in a city from the families a real mission would use: social chatter and local news reporting (two streams over one feed, the second promoted to its own banding family), inbound charter and display aviation, lodging scarcity near the venue, and rental fleet drawdown at the airport.

APIDIRECT.unit_basis: One unit per HTTP request. Twitter bills per PAGE, so a pages=2 call is two billable pages inside one request — the ledger counts requests and would under-count a multi-page call.
APIDIRECT.retention_basis: No retention term published by the vendor, so the window is OURS to choose rather than one we were granted. The shipped config asks for 90 days — long enough that a 14-day baseline stays re-derivable.
APIDIRECT.provenance: Aggregator. The posts are X/Twitter's, Reddit's and news publishers' content; API Direct is an intermediary and its terms do not displace theirs.

failure_modes.401: bad or missing key — raises, never an empty list
failure_modes.429: rate limited — not observed at our volume
failure_modes.5xx: vendor fault — raises; the query is FAILED and becomes a coverage gap
failure_modes.200 with []: a genuine absence of results, and the ONLY case that may be read as one

measured.news_time_published: 1d returned ZERO for this lexicon; 7d works

FR24.unit_basis: Credits per RECORD RETURNED, not per request. /live/flight-positions/full costs 8 per flight returned and a flat 1 for an empty response, so `limit` is not a cost control and units must be computed AFTER the response arrives.
FR24.retention_basis: Contractual. The vendor's storage rules require permanent deletion within 30 days of first receipt, uniformly across endpoints. This is a CEILING: config may shorten it and cannot extend it.
FR24.provenance: Primary collector. FR24 aggregates ADS-B from its own receiver network; the positions are its data, which is why it is the one provider with an explicit retention term we are bound by.

rate_limits.measured: Explorer: 10/min, burst ceiling of ONE — two calls 0.2s apart returned 429

failure_modes.402: credit exhaustion — DISTINCT from 429 and the reason the two are handled separately
failure_modes.429: rate limit — prevented by the token bucket, not retried into
failure_modes.403: endpoint not on this tier (the /count tripwire on Explorer)

measured.category_on_live_positions: ABSENT — 22 fields, none of them `category`, so M cannot be proven from a live position

PRICELINE.unit_basis: One unit per request, any endpoint. RapidAPI plans are limitType: hard with zero overage at every tier, so exhaustion cuts access off rather than billing.
PRICELINE.retention_basis: No retention term published, so the window is ours to choose. The shipped config asks for 90 days.
PRICELINE.provenance: Aggregator over rental partners (Avis, Hertz, Alamo and others) via RapidAPI. Two intermediaries deep: RapidAPI resells Priceline, which aggregates the partners. As of 8.5 the reseller is `priceline-com2`; the upstream and therefore the rights position are unchanged.

failure_modes.400: Zod validation — carries an issues[] array naming the field
failure_modes.quota exhausted: hard cutoff, not an overage charge
failure_modes.missing vehicles[] field: SchemaError, never a substituted zero — a silent zero in an availability count reads as scarcity
failure_modes.200 with totalResultsAvailable 0: INDISTINGUISHABLE from a sold-out market on one call, so it is judged on the BASELINE window: a baseline with zero total availability establishes no normal level and gives no denominator, and is raised as PlatformUnavailableError rather than recorded as a zero drop.

measured.daily_price_fields: dailyPrice and strikeDailyPrice were both 0 while totalPrice was populated — derive from totalPrice/numRentalDays
measured.itemKey_stability: encodes the pickup/dropoff datetimes, so it CANNOT join a near-term offer to its baseline; identity is (partner.code, code, pickupLocation.locationId)
measured.health_check_endpoint: the probe calls the CAR SEARCH path, not autocomplete. On priceline8 autocomplete returned 500 while search worked, so the cheap probe reported the family down while it was up; probing search also means the check would have caught the 8.5 outage, where search was what broke.
measured.offers_per_search: 272 offers -> 71 CAR signals in 2 requests (first live run, priceline8 wrapper)
measured.zero_inventory_2026_08_09: the priceline8 wrapper returned success:true with totalResultsAvailable 0 for every PHX and JFK window at +1/+2/+7/+14 days. Before 8.3 that read as full coverage of a quiet market.
measured.wrapper_swap_2026_08_10: priceline-com2 serves the SAME upstream unchanged — 510 vehicles near / 758 baseline at PHX, with peopleCapacity, counterType and partner intact. The outage was wrapper-side, not upstream (8.5).
measured.rate_plan_duplication: the SAME car is listed once per rate plan — identical `id`, differing only in `rate`/`groupId`/`score`. Measured: 510 rows for 348 distinct ids. Offers are de-duplicated on `id`, because counting rows made an extra price point look like extra inventory and a trimmed price list look like scarcity.
measured.vehiclesFinal: NOT a de-duplicated list, despite the name. It held 170 of 494 retail offers plus 16 opaque `express` deals that carry no partner. Keying on it undercounted availability by about two thirds and produced offer keys with an unknown supplier.
measured.offer_identity: `id` (e.g. PFAR-R-HZ-PHX-HZ-PHX-CC) is date-free and stable across windows: 311 of 348/560 ids shared between the near and baseline windows. `itemKey` is NOT — only 7 shared, because it encodes the datetimes.
measured.distance_units: MILES, not kilometres. Measured against the counters' own coordinates: every PHX counter matched the great-circle distance in miles. Converted before it reaches `distance_km` and a 15 KM spatial gate.

STAYING.unit_basis: Credits per call, REPORTED not inferrable. meta.creditsCharged is authoritative and sits beside `data`, so an unwrap that reads only `data` loses it.
STAYING.retention_basis: No retention term published, so the window is ours to choose. The shipped config asks for 90 days.
STAYING.provenance: Aggregator over Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo and Google Hotels. Listings, prices and host details belong to those platforms and their hosts.

failure_modes.202: asynchronous job — poll /jobs/{id} honouring Retry-After. Not an error.
failure_modes.platform status 'skipped': a requested platform did not run. MUST raise — the vendor confirmed by email that a Google validation failure had been normalised into an ok/0-results leg, which is a failure wearing the costume of a search.

measured.calendar_coverage: ~1 listing in 40 returned calendar data against a floor of 3 paired listings
measured.vrbo: every availability flag False even 30 days out

geography.resolution: city or county name, resolved to airport codes
geography.unmapped_city_effect: FLIGHT and CAR report SKIPPED_NO_MAPPING — an absent source, never an absent signal

retention.basis: FlightRadar24 licence requires deletion within 30 days; the analytical record outlives the payload with a nulled pointer

limitations: 'Nowheresville, ZZ' does not resolve to a known city (UNRESOLVED); flight and car collection have no airport to key on. Social still works, so the jurisdiction is partially covered rather than unusable.
LODGING depends on key_locations registered for the session, and on Staying returning calendar data — measured at roughly 1 listing in 40.

open_rights_questions.provenance: Aggregator. The posts are X/Twitter's, Reddit's and news publishers' content; API Direct is an intermediary and its terms do not displace theirs.
open_rights_questions.question: UNRESOLVED. Post text and author handles are third-party content redistributed through an aggregator. The system returns snippets in alert evidence because the snippet IS the evidence — an alert its reader cannot check is not an alert — but no term has been produced that grants redistribution. This is the largest open rights question in the system and it is not closed by the fact that the vendor served the bytes.

open_rights_questions.provenance: Primary collector. FR24 aggregates ADS-B from its own receiver network; the positions are its data, which is why it is the one provider with an explicit retention term we are bound by.
open_rights_questions.question: Retention is explicit and enforced in code. Redistribution of positions in alert evidence is NOT explicitly granted; the system returns normalised flight facts (callsign, type, ETA) rather than raw position payloads, which narrows the exposure without resolving the question.

open_rights_questions.provenance: Aggregator over rental partners (Avis, Hertz, Alamo and others) via RapidAPI. Two intermediaries deep: RapidAPI resells Priceline, which aggregates the partners. As of 8.5 the reseller is `priceline-com2`; the upstream and therefore the rights position are unchanged.
open_rights_questions.question: UNRESOLVED. The system stores counts and class-level aggregates rather than bookable offers, and checkoutUrl/detailsKey are dropped before storage because they are booking capability, not evidence. Partner pricing is the partners' commercial data.

open_rights_questions.provenance: Aggregator over Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo and Google Hotels. Listings, prices and host details belong to those platforms and their hosts.
open_rights_questions.question: UNRESOLVED, and the exposure is narrower than it looks: the system stores and returns availability COUNTS and price aggregates, not listing content, images or host identities. No term has been produced granting redistribution of the underlying platforms' listing data, and the aggregator's licence does not speak for Airbnb's.

caveats: Confidence scores are a starting hypothesis, not a calibrated probability. Do not present them to a decision-maker as one.
Sensitivity floors are interim and set from a single model's measurements.
Coverage is US-only and keyed on airport mappings.
